question.text: The Market-Cap-to-GDP ratio of the Indian equity market is currently around 70%. Per textbook interpretation, the market is:

explanation.text: The Logic: Interpretation table: <50% Undervalued, 50–75% Moderately Undervalued, 75–90% Fairly Valued, 90–110% Moderately Overvalued, >110% Overvalued. 70% falls in the 'Moderately Undervalued' band. The Trap: Off-by-one bucket error — students often pick 'Fairly Valued' for 70% because it feels 'normal'. Cross-Exam Context: XV Ch 5 (Economic Analysis) covers this as Buffett Indicator; XXI-B uses it for tactical allocation decisions. Manager's Pro-Tip: The ratio is a blunt instrument — treat bands as guidance, not triggers. Buffett himself caveats with interest-rate context.
